title_prefix: Eviction netgroup secret is drawn at loa
mechanism: CONFIRMED, and stronger than the finding states. src/node/eviction.lisp:92 is (defvar *eviction-netgroup-secret* (random most-positive-fixnum)); a defvar initform is evaluated at LOAD time. seed-global-random-state is called only at the head of init-node (src/node/init.lisp:11-17), i.e. inside start-node, long after the file has loaded, and it does not touch an already-bound defvar. SBCL 2.6.5's initial CL:*RANDOM-STATE* is a build-time constant, so the draw is a process constant. The deployed launcher (scripts/run-node.sh, the sbcl line with --eval '(asdf:load-system :bitcoin-lisp)') is a FRESH sbcl loading FASLs on every restart, not the saved core, so the save-lisp-and-die freeze in scripts/build-node-core.lisp is only one of two ways to reach the same constant - the FASL-load path reaches it too. The ASDF load consumes ZERO draws from *random-state* before eviction.lisp, so the 'secret' is exactly the FIRST (random most-positive-fixnum) of a bare sbcl of that version: an attacker needs neither the repository nor the binary. %evict-keyed-netgroup (eviction.lisp:83-90) is then (sxhash (cons SECRET group)), a plain deterministic SBCL hash. Core instead draws nSeed0/nSeed1 per process from a default-constructed FastRandomContext (OS-seeded ChaCha20) at AppInitMain (refs/bitcoin/src/init.cpp:1642-1648) and keys SipHash-2-4 with them (refs/bitcoin/src/net.cpp:4131-4141, RANDOMIZER_ID_NETGROUP at net.cpp:110). Secondary defect found while probing: sxhash is not avalanching, so keyed values cluster by netgroup string prefix - the offline top 10 of all 57,088 /16 netgroups were 190.210 through 190.219, one contiguous block.
consequence: REAL BUT BOUNDED - severity downgraded S1 -> S2. The pass the secret protects is +evict-protect-netgroup+ = 4 candidates out of *max-inbound-connections* = 114 (Core's 125-11 default; src/node/params.lisp:84, set by automatic-inbound-capacity at init.lisp:373). Executed end to end with a positive control: 40 honest inbound peers in distinct /16s with good ping and recent tx/blocks, plus 4 attacker peers made the WORST candidate on every other metric (min-ping 99999, last-tx 0, last-block 0, newest connect-time). With the attacker sitting in the offline top-4 netgroups (190.217/190.218/190.215/190.216, keys ~4.611e18 vs honest max 1.733e18): 24 evictions, 0 attacker peers evicted, all 4 surviving. Same peers moved to the 4 LOWEST-ranked netgroups: all 4 evicted. So the netgroup pass alone is what saves them and the choice is entirely attacker-controlled. Cost: 4 connections, one address in each of 4 chosen /16s; with an unpredictable key the same 4 connections own all 4 protected slots with probability 1/C(44,4) = 1/135,751 (~7.4e-6), and an attacker would otherwise have to own nearly all 114 inbound slots to occupy the top 4 reliably. What it does NOT buy: (1) no ban/discourage bypass - merge-inbound-peers (eviction.lisp:12-36) calls evict-discouraged-inbound BEFORE evict-least-valuable-inbound and that function ignores every protection pass, and inbound-connection-allowed-p (eviction.lisp:311-351) drops banned addresses at accept and discouraged ones once the slots are near full, so the immortal slots must be held by well-behaved peers; (2) no scaling - k is hard-capped at 4, and slots 5+ require beating the min-ping 8, tx 4, block-relay-only 8, block 4 and the connection-age ratio pass, none of which read the secret and all of which are equally deterministic in Core, so they are not a divergence; (3) not an eclipse - 4 of 114 inbound slots (3.5%) and 0 of the node's 8-10 self-chosen outbound connections, which are what carry headers and blocks. The deployed mainnet node runs :listen nil (scripts/run-node.sh mainnet START_OPTS) so it accepts no inbound at all; testnet4 listens with the 114 default. Verdict: a genuine, cheap, fully deterministic divergence from Core that should be fixed, but it is not the eclipse lever an S1 requires.
evidence: All probes ran in the pinned project container (scripts/docker-sbcl.sh, SBCL 2.6.5.HEAD.1-85913ed). (1) Build-time RNG is a process constant: three fresh `sbcl --no-userinit --no-sysinit` runs each printed BUILDTIME-RNG (113500 2499109626526694126 2.6.5.HEAD.1-85913ed). (2) Production launch path reproduced four times - fresh sbcl + (asdf:load-system "bitcoin-lisp") + print: run 1 (cold FASL volume, compiles) secret=1695793585479058544; runs 2, 3 and 4 (pure FASL load, which is what every restart does because run-node.sh clears the cache only on a git-rev change) secret=1193941380623146742 IDENTICALLY, with seedvar=NIL every time (seed-global-random-state has not run at load). (3) No repository needed: a bare `sbcl --no-userinit --no-sysinit` printed first-fixnum-draw=1193941380623146742, the same value. (4) Offline computability: the same bare sbcl printed sxhash-cons-1-2=3381451751480243550, and inside the loaded node %evict-keyed-netgroup on a peer at 1.2.3.4 returned 3381451751480243550 - END-TO-END match=T. (5) Startup does not repair it: BEFORE-SEED secret=1193941380623146742 seedvar=NIL; after calling bitcoin-lisp::seed-global-random-state, AFTER-SEED secret=1193941380623146742 seedvar-set=yes. (6) Attack + positive control through the shipped selector bitcoin-lisp::select-inbound-peer-to-evict: RESULT CHOSEN-TOP4: pool=44 evicted=24 attacker-evicted=0 attacker-surviving=4; RESULT CONTROL-BOTTOM4: pool=44 evicted=24 attacker-evicted=4 attacker-surviving=0. (7) Constants read from the image: PROTECT-K netgroup=4 min-ping=8 tx=4 block-relay-only=8 block=4 max-inbound=114. (8) sxhash clustering: str-sxhash("190.215")=2844009626900421855, ("190.216")=2844009626917199474, ("190.217")=2844009626933977093 - differing only in low bits; SEARCH-SPACE 57088 netgroups, TOP12 all in 190.210-190.238. Files: src/node/eviction.lisp:83-97 (%evict-keyed-netgroup and the defvar), :56-58 (+evict-protect-netgroup+ = 4), :205-215 (the netgroup pass inside select-inbound-peer-to-evict), :12-36 (merge-inbound-peers ordering), :311-351 (inbound-connection-allowed-p); src/node/init.lisp:11-17 and :373; src/node/entropy.lisp:33-61; src/node/params.lisp:84; scripts/run-node.sh (the sbcl --eval '(asdf:load-system :bitcoin-lisp)' launch line) and scripts/build-node-core.lisp:16-29; Core refs/bitcoin/src/init.cpp:1642-1648, refs/bitcoin/src/net.cpp:110 and :4131-4141, refs/bitcoin/src/node/eviction.cpp:178-205.
fix_shape: Do not leave the value to a load-time initform. Declare the variable unbound (or NIL) at load time and draw it inside the startup path, the way Core constructs CConnman with rng.rand64() twice at AppInitMain: set *eviction-netgroup-secret* from the OS CSPRNG in init-node, next to (and after) seed-global-random-state, using the same source that %os-entropy-seed already uses (ironclad:random-data, i.e. getrandom(2)/urandom) rather than CL:random, so it is independent of *random-state* entirely and cannot be replayed by re-running the loader; a NIL value reaching %evict-keyed-netgroup should be a hard error, not a silent fallback, so the wiring cannot be dropped again. While there, replace (sxhash (cons secret group)) with a real keyed PRF over the raw netgroup bytes - Core uses SipHash-2-4 keyed with two 64-bit words and a domain separator (RANDOMIZER_ID_NETGROUP), and the tree already has the primitives - because sxhash is not avalanching and lets netgroups that share a prefix cluster to adjacent keys, which weakens the pass even with an unpredictable secret. Grep confirms this is the ONLY defvar/defparameter in src/ whose initform calls CL:random (the other load-time entropy draws, src/coalton/interop.lisp:483 and src/mempool/spanning-forest.lisp:723, already use ironclad:random-data and are unaffected), so no second site needs the same treatment. Add a test that asserts the secret differs between two independently seeded startups and that it is not equal to a fresh process's first (random most-positive-fixnum). NOT IMPLEMENTED - verdict only.
